transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… my regular doctor thought I should come talk to someone. She says I’ve gotten too thin. I don’t know, I guess my work pants are hanging pretty loose lately, so maybe she’s right.

It’s not that I’m trying to be difficult or anything… but when the number on the scale is lower, part of me feels kind of relieved. I know that probably sounds strange.
Do you ever worry about gaining weight?

I mean… yes, I suppose I do. Not all the time, but if I eat something heavier—like biscuits or pasta—I get nervous afterward. I’ll keep thinking, “Is that going to show on me?” and I end up checking myself the rest of the day.

I know that may sound silly… I just feel like I need to make up for it somehow. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour?

I don’t think so… not like a big amount all at once. I mean, I might pick at something here or there, but within an hour, like really a lot? No, I can’t say I’ve noticed that happening. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt upset after eating sometimes, but I don’t go and make myself throw up. I wouldn’t want to do that. Is that what you were asking?
Do you limit the types or amounts of food you eat?

I… yes, I suppose I do, though I try not to make a fuss about it. I cook proper plates for my husband and my mother-in-law, you know, normal meals. But by the time I sit down myself, I usually think, well, coffee is enough, or just a few vegetables… maybe half a piece of toast.

It doesn’t feel like I’m doing anything drastic in the moment. I tell myself I don’t need much. Is that what you mean by limiting?
Do you think about your weight throughout the day?

I wouldn’t say it’s all day exactly… but yes, it does come up a lot. I notice how I look, especially around my stomach. If I feel small and neat, I feel like I’m doing okay, like I’ve got things under control.

But if I look in the mirror and my stomach seems even a little full, I get this awful feeling like I’ve let myself go. I know that probably sounds silly… but that’s how it feels.
Do you think you would be extremely upset if you gained a small amount of weight?

I… yes, I think I would be upset. Maybe more than I should be, if I’m honest.

If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I can spend the rest of the day worrying it’s going to show on me. I keep sort of checking myself, and thinking I need to make up for it somehow. I know a small amount probably shouldn’t matter that much… but it feels like it does.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?

I don’t think so… not in the way people mean, I suppose. I’m usually quite careful, maybe too careful, so it’s hard to imagine really losing control.

There are times I feel uncomfortable after eating something I hadn’t planned, but I wouldn’t call it a binge or anything like that. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past few months?

I suppose… yes, there has been some weight loss. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but my doctor did say I’ve gotten too thin.

And I’ve noticed my work pants are hanging looser on me than they used to. Part of me knows that should worry me, but… if I’m being honest, when the number on the scale is lower, I still feel a bit relieved. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Is your decision to limit the food you eat mostly driven by a fear of gaining weight?

Mostly, yes… though I don’t like saying it that plainly.

If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I can get scared it’s going to show on me, and then I spend the rest of the day checking myself or thinking I should make up for it somehow. I know that probably sounds a bit silly, but yes… I think fear of gaining weight is a big part of why I limit things.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle?

Oh… well, I’m not really sure that applies to me now, at my age. I don’t have periods anymore, so I can’t say I’ve noticed changes in that way.

Is that what you meant, or were you asking more generally about hormones and things?
Have you had periods of time where you gained back the weight you had lost?

Not really, no… I mean, not in any lasting way. My doctor keeps saying I’ve gotten too thin, and I can see it too, with my work pants hanging loose.

But I suppose part of me still feels… pleased, or relieved, when the number on the scale is lower. I know that may not be the right way to look at it.
Do you think you look overweight even when others tell you that you are too thin?

I wouldn’t say I think I look… exactly overweight, no. But I don’t see what other people seem to see either.

When I’m small and neat-looking, I feel like I’m managing myself properly, if that makes sense. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little full, I feel like I’ve let myself go. I know that may sound a bit harsh, and I’m not trying to be difficult… that’s just how it feels to me.
Have you ever had a time when you gained back a significant amount of weight after losing it?

No, not a significant amount, I don’t think. My doctor keeps saying I’ve gotten too thin, and I can see my work pants are hanging loose on me.

I suppose… I haven’t really gained it back, not in a way that lasts. And I feel a little embarrassed saying this, but part of me still feels relieved when the scale is lower. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Do you think you look fat even when you are at a weight that others consider too thin?

I don’t know if I’d say “fat,” exactly… that feels a little strong. But when I’m small and neat-looking, I feel like I’m handling things the right way.

If I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full, I do feel like I’ve let myself go. I know that probably isn’t the best way to think about it, but… yes, that’s how it feels to me.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict what you eat?

I suppose it is part of it, yes… though I don’t like saying it that bluntly.

If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I can spend the rest of the day worrying it’s going to show on me. Then I keep checking myself, or thinking I ought to make up for it somehow. I know that probably sounds silly, but that fear is definitely there.
Do you feel your self-worth is closely tied to your weight?

I suppose it is, more than I like to admit.

When I stay small and neat-looking, I feel like I’m… doing things properly, like I’ve got myself together. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach seems even a little full, I feel like I’ve let myself go. I know that probably sounds vain or silly, but it does affect how I feel about myself.
Do you think your weight is the most important aspect of your appearance?

Maybe not the most important… I don’t want to sound as if that’s all I care about.

But yes, it does matter a lot to me. When I stay small and neat-looking, I feel like I’m handling everything right. And if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full, I feel like I’ve let myself go. I know that probably isn’t a very sensible way to judge myself, but that’s how it feels.
Is your fear of gaining weight the only reason you limit your food intake?

I don’t think it’s the only reason… or at least, I don’t want to make it sound too simple.

But it is a big part of it. If I have something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I can get frightened it’s going to show on me somehow. Then I’m checking myself and thinking I should make up for it. I know that may not sound very reasonable, but that’s what happens.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you eat as little as you do?

Yes… I think it probably is the main reason, if I’m being honest.

I try not to make it sound dramatic, but if I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I spend the rest of the day worrying it’s going to show on me somehow. Then I keep checking myself and thinking I ought to make up for it. I know that may not sound very sensible, but that’s what goes through my mind.
